findings.title: Monthly SEC XBRL workflow produces output that nothing consumes and nothing stores
findings.description: The monthly workflow pulls up to 1500 SEC companyfacts files (~6 GB transient) into external-data/sec-xbrl/, which is gitignored ('external-data/sec-xbrl/*.json' in .gitignore) and lives on an ephemeral GitHub runner. Only _manifest.json is committed. A repo-wide grep for 'xbrl'/'companyfacts'/'sec-xbrl' shows ZERO consumers outside the puller itself, its UA test, and comments: no engine method, no generate-* script, no snapshot-* script ever reads the company-facts data OR the committed manifest. The puller's own header (pull-sec-xbrl.js:10-12) says 'Diese PR macht NUR den Pull. Das Merge-In-Snapshots passiert in einem Folge-PR' — that follow-up was never built (Tag 133k era; codebase is now at Tag 246, months later).
findings.mechanism: Data written to gitignored dir on ephemeral runner -> runner destroyed at job end -> data evaporates. Committed manifest is read by no consumer. Workflow has run monthly for months performing pure dead work, and its 'Verify SEC Coverage' gate green-lights a dataset that ceases to exist seconds later.
findings.reproducer: grep -rln 'sec-xbrl\|companyfacts\|xbrl' --include='*.js' . | grep -v node_modules  -> only pull-sec-xbrl.js, tests/sec-user-agent-test.js, scripts/pull-insider-form4.js (comment-only), lib/atomic-write.js (comment-only). Then: cat .gitignore | grep sec-xbrl.
findings.impact: Monthly runner time, SEC bandwidth, and maintenance effort (UA-guard test, coverage gate, cherry-pick push hardening — all Tag 218/232c work) invested in a workflow whose entire data product is discarded. Worse: the committed manifest creates the illusion that XBRL fundamentals coverage exists.
findings.suggested_fix: Decide: either (a) build the snapshot-merge consumer and persist the cache (actions/cache or a separate data branch / external storage), or (b) disable the workflow until the consumer exists. Do not keep paying the monthly cost for a no-op.

findings.title: SEC pull processes the SAME first 1500 CIKs every month; 304s count as coverage of data that does not exist
findings.description: Two compounding defects in the bounded-slice design. (1) pull-sec-xbrl.js:125 'const todo = entries.slice(0, args.max)' takes the first 1500 entries of the (stably ordered) SEC ticker list on every scheduled run — there is no rotation offset, so CIKs 1501..~9900 are NEVER touched by a scheduled run, contradicting the workflow comment 'Bound each scheduled run to a disk/time-safe slice' which implies coverage accumulates. (2) The puller sends If-Modified-Since from the COMMITTED manifest (prior.lastModified); SEC answers 304; the code takes the res.notModified branch and writes NO file (pull-sec-xbrl.js:138-140) — yet the workflow's Verify SEC Coverage gate counts 304s as 'ok' ('const ok = pulled + c304 + fresh', monthly-sec-xbrl.yml:101). On an ephemeral runner a 304 means zero bytes of data exist anywhere, but coverage reports healthy.
findings.mechanism: Stable list order + slice(0, max) + manifest-driven conditional GET + ephemeral cache = after the first month, most of the slice returns 304, the gate passes, and effectively nothing is ever downloaded again — for the same 1500 tickers, forever.
findings.reproducer: Read pull-sec-xbrl.js:124-141. Run twice with empty cache dir but committed manifest present: second run reports skipped304>>pulled with no files written.
findings.impact: Even if a consumer existed (F-CI-001), scheduled runs could never deliver more than ~15% of the SEC universe, and after run 1 mostly deliver nothing while reporting success.
findings.suggested_fix: Persist a rotation cursor in the manifest (e.g. lastOffset) and slice(cursor, cursor+max) with wraparound; only count 'pulled' (file actually written this run) toward coverage when the cache is known-ephemeral.

findings.title: Staleness rotation is a no-op in CI: snapshots/ and fundamentals-cache/ are gitignored, runner starts empty
findings.description: The 13% coverage-gate calibration (Tag 233 comment, daily-pull.yml:349: 'sorted by staleness, so stale tickers rotate through across days') rests on a false premise in CI. sortByStaleness() (pull-yahoo.js:1265) derives each ticker's age from its snapshot file in the output dir — but snapshots/ is gitignored ('Tag 151: regenerated fresh every run'), so on a fresh runner every ticker has age=0 and the stable sort preserves the watchlist order, which refresh-universe.js:444 sorts ALPHABETICALLY by ticker ('wlRaw.stocks.sort((a,b)=>a.ticker.localeCompare(b.ticker))'). Empirics: the bot-committed picks-history/2026-06-12.json spans A-Z, so full traversal does complete on good days — but on timeout-truncated runs (manifest partial=true, e.g. run 26022734084 with n_ok=4613) the unprocessed tail is ALWAYS the alphabet end, and no state survives to prioritize those tickers next run. Additionally FUNDAMENTALS_MAX_AGE_DAYS='7' (daily-pull.yml:203) is dead config in CI: fundamentals-cache/ is also gitignored and there is no actions/cache restore step, so every run does a FULL fundamentals pull for every ticker — the price-only fast path ('oldest first -> full pull, recent -> price-only', pull-yahoo.js:88) never triggers. This is a major contributor to the 163-min pull times and rate-limit storms the workflow comments fight (Tag 215f, Tag 219).
findings.mechanism: Tag 151 (stop committing snapshots) silently broke Tag 164 (staleness rotation reads snapshot mtimes) and the incremental-pull architecture; subsequent gate recalibrations (Tag 207b, 215e, 233) treated the symptom (low coverage %) while documenting a rotation that cannot occur on CI.
findings.reproducer: git ls-files snapshots -> only _manifest.json. Read pull-yahoo.js sortByStaleness: fs.existsSync(snapshot) false for all -> ageCache all 0 -> stable sort no-op. Watchlist order: node -e check shows 000270.KS ... ZZZOF (alphabetical).
findings.impact: On partial runs, late-alphabet tickers (S-Z, ~25% of the 23,748 universe) are systematically dropped with no catch-up mechanism; coverage holes are deterministic, not rotating. Every run re-downloads full fundamentals for the whole universe, wasting ~2h of the 240-min budget and provoking Yahoo throttling.
findings.suggested_fix: Persist rotation state cheaply: either restore snapshots/ (or just a tiny per-ticker lastPulled index file, committed) before the pull, or add actions/cache for fundamentals-cache/ keyed by week, or have pull-yahoo read per-ticker lastPulled from a committed compact index and write it back. Then re-validate the 13% gate.

findings.title: Repo bloat trajectory: ~125 MB of committed artifacts churned per run, .git at 553 MB after ~1 month
findings.description: The daily commit ('git add -A') rewrites alert-state.json (44.3 MB) and method-history-state.json (55.8 MB — already past GitHub's 50 MB push-warning threshold) every run, and adds a NEW methods-history/<date>.json that grew from 18.0 MB (2026-06-08) to 25.7 MB (2026-06-10/12) — a 43% jump in two days, tracking universe growth toward the MAX_UNIVERSE=25000 cap. With --methods-keep-days 90 the working tree converges to ~90 x 25.7 MB ≈ 2.3 GB of committed methods-history alone; git history grows without bound (deleted files stay in history). Local .git is already 553 MB. checkout uses fetch-depth: 0, so EVERY daily run clones the full, ever-growing history. The Archive Old Snapshots step that is supposed to bound this is continue-on-error: true with no follow-up sanity gate (unlike refresh/prune which got Verify Watchlist Sanity), so repeated silent archive failures would let methods-history grow past 90 files with zero signal.
findings.mechanism: Daily blob churn (44+55 MB state rewrites compress poorly as JSON deltas across full-file value changes) + 25.7 MB/day of brand-new history files + full-history checkout = compounding cost: slower checkouts, slower pushes, and a hard stop if any single file crosses GitHub's 100 MB block (method-history-state.json is the candidate: 8.9 MB at Tag ~190 per detect-changes.js comment, 55.8 MB today; bounded mainly by universe size and method count — adding methods or raising MAX_UNIVERSE pushes it toward 100 MB, at which point the daily push fails permanently).
findings.reproducer: git ls-files -z methods-history | xargs -0 du -cb -> 506 MB across 28 files; ls -la alert-state.json method-history-state.json; du -sh .git -> 553M; git log --author=yahoo-pull-bot --stat -1.
findings.impact: Within months: multi-GB repo, multi-minute checkouts inside a budget-constrained job (compounds F-CI-006), push-time warnings, and an eventual hard 100 MB block that kills the daily pipeline. GitHub also throttles/contacts owners of multi-GB repos.
findings.suggested_fix: Move bulky state off main: (a) shard method-history-state.json per ticker-prefix or store as gitignored runner artifact restored via actions/cache, (b) write methods-history vintages straight to the gitignored ndjson archive (or a dedicated data branch with periodic history rewrite / git-lfs), (c) add a size gate after Archive Old Snapshots (fail if methods-history file count > 95 or any state file > 80 MB).

findings.title: Manual-dispatch concurrency escape hatch guarantees unresolvable conflict when overlapping the cron run
findings.description: Tag 219a gives workflow_dispatch runs a per-run concurrency group ('manual-{run_id}') so operators can run while a scheduled pull is in flight. But both runs rewrite the SAME files (alert-state.json, method-history-state.json, methods-history/<RUN_DATE>.json — both runs freeze the same RUN_DATE_UTC). Whichever run pushes second hits a rebase content conflict on these JSONs; the recovery path is: rebase fails -> abort -> 'git reset --hard origin/main' + 'git cherry-pick $COMMIT_SHA' — but the cherry-pick replays the IDENTICAL content conflict and fails -> exit 1. The cherry-pick fallback can only rescue 'rebase lost the commit' scenarios, never a genuine same-file conflict.
findings.mechanism: Concurrency exemption -> parallel writers of the same monolithic state files -> rebase AND cherry-pick both deterministically fail -> the slower run exits 1 after ~4h of work, and because snapshots are runner-local (F-CI-003), its entire dataset is discarded, not merely delayed.
findings.reproducer: Trigger workflow_dispatch while the scheduled run is between Checkout and Commit; observe the loser's Commit step fail with 'cherry-pick failed'. Two manual overlapping-day runs already occurred (bot commits 2026-05-13 04:25+05:09, 2026-05-19 14:55+19:41).
findings.impact: Any manual re-run that overlaps the cron run converts one of the two runs into total data loss for the day (visible as a red run, but ~4h of pull burned). Operator intuition says 'manual run is safe'; it is not.
findings.suggested_fix: Either share the 'main-push' group for dispatch too (queueing is annoying but safe), or gate the manual run's Commit step on a lock check (e.g. skip state-file commit and only refresh reports when a cron run is in flight), or make state files mergeable (per-ticker shards make conflicts disjoint).

findings.title: Single end-of-job commit + over-committed step budgets: ~19% of days produce NO data commit
findings.description: Everything the run produces is committed in ONE step at minute ~200+ of a 240-min job. Worst-case pre-commit arithmetic: pre-pull steps can consume ~60 min (Refresh Universe 20 + Insider Form-4 30 + FX 5 + npm/tests) + Yahoo Pull 165 = 225 of 240, leaving 15 min for a downstream chain whose own step budgets sum to >80 min (Earnings 20 + Historical Prices 25 + Walk-Forward 15 + Sector-Medians 10 + Method-Effectiveness 10 + reports + commit). When the job-level timeout SIGKILLs before 'Commit Snapshots', the ENTIRE day is lost because snapshots/fundamentals-cache are runner-local (F-CI-003) — exactly the Run #108 post-mortem failure mode (comment at line 26-32), which the 180->240 raise mitigated but did not bound. Empirics: yahoo-pull-bot commits are missing for 6 of the last 31 days (05-16, 05-18, 05-27, 06-03, 06-09, 06-11); picks-history confirms vintage gaps (no 2026-06-09/06-11 files). Bot commits land 09:16-10:32 UTC, i.e. runs routinely consume nearly the full budget (cron 02:00 + delay + ~4h runtime).
findings.mechanism: No checkpoint commit exists between 'pull finished + gates passed' and 'all 15 report/analytics steps done'. Any job-level kill (timeout, runner eviction, infra flake) in the ~40-60 min report phase discards the expensive, already-validated pull data along with the cheap, regenerable reports.
findings.reproducer: git log --since=2026-05-12 --author=yahoo-pull-bot --format='%ad' --date=short | sort -u -> 25 distinct days of 31. ls picks-history -> gaps at 06-09, 06-11. Sum the per-step timeout-minutes vs timeout-minutes: 240.
findings.impact: Walk-forward perf, method-effectiveness, and picks/methods vintage series silently accumulate holes (their week-offset lookups must fuzzy-match or drop those dates); ~1 day in 5 of Yahoo pull effort (≈4h runner time + full universe fundamentals download) is thrown away.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an intermediate 'Commit Pull Data' step immediately after Verify Pull Coverage (snapshots manifest, picks/methods/score history inputs are not yet built then — so commit at least watchlist/fx/insider/earnings + run a second commit at the end), or better: move the report chain into a separate job (needs artifact handoff) so the data commit is not hostage to report runtime. Also subtract observed pre-pull worst case from the pull's 165-min step timeout dynamically.

findings.title: Health-check allowlist misses generate-screener: crash deploys stale screener.html with 404ing detail payload
findings.description: pipeline-health-check.js's EXPECTED_SCRIPTS allowlist (the F-CI-002 'missing report = 100% fail' rule) covers only snapshot-picks, snapshot-methods-history, generate-modes-report, snapshot-score-history. generate-screener.js — producer of the primary 6-tab dashboard (Tag 198) — is NOT on the list, nor are generate-dashboard, generate-diff-report, pick-diff, walk-forward-perf, method-effectiveness, detect-changes, snapshot-r40rx-history. If generate-screener.js crashes on line 1 (continue-on-error: true), the health check still passes and Deploy runs. Deploy then publishes (a) screener.html restored from checkout — yesterday's committed version, no staleness banner — and (b) NO screener-detail.json, because that file is gitignored ('cp screener-detail.json _site/ 2>/dev/null || true' silently no-ops) and the gh-pages force-push replaces the whole tree, deleting the previous deploy's copy.
findings.mechanism: Tracked HTML artifacts act as invisible stale fallbacks (checkout restores them), defeating missing-file detection; the gitignored heavy payload has no such fallback, so the live site ends up INTERNALLY INCONSISTENT: yesterday's table renders, but every detail-modal fetch('screener-detail.json') 404s.
findings.reproducer: Simulate: exit 1 at top of generate-screener.js; run the workflow; health check passes (no screener entry in EXPECTED_SCRIPTS); _site contains stale screener.html and no screener-detail.json; gh-pages force-push removes the old detail payload.
findings.impact: User-facing dashboard silently serves day-old picks with broken modals — precisely the 'silently publishing yesterday's HTML masks real breakage' failure the Tag 134 hard-fail policy was written to prevent.
findings.suggested_fix: Add generate-screener (and ideally generate-diff-report, detect-changes, snapshot-r40rx-history) to EXPECTED_SCRIPTS with health-report emission; in the Deploy step, hard-fail if screener.html's embedded generation timestamp is older than RUN_DATE_UTC, and fail (not '|| true') when screener-detail.json is absent while screener.html is being deployed.

findings.title: detect-changes soft-fail leaves alert/trend state stale with no health-check coverage
findings.description: Detect Changes + Discord-Alert runs with continue-on-error: true and is not in the health-check EXPECTED_SCRIPTS allowlist. If detect-changes.js crashes (e.g. on a corrupt alert-state.json — the exact scenario Tag 232a-2 documents), the run stays green: alert-state.json and method-history-state.json are simply not updated, Discord change-alerts silently stop, and the methodHistory trend series (Trend.appendHistory window) gets a hole. On the NEXT successful run, diffs are computed against 2-day-old state, double-reporting every change that happened in between as 'new today' — polluting the alert stream and the lastChanged dates that downstream pick-diff/trend logic consumes.
findings.mechanism: Soft-fail without a watchdog: the step's only failure signal is a log line inside a green run; the committed state files' staleness is invisible because they are re-committed unchanged by 'git add -A'.
findings.reproducer: Corrupt alert-state.json locally, run the workflow steps in order: detect-changes exits non-zero, workflow continues, commit step commits old state, health check passes.
findings.impact: Silent gap in the change-alert stream (the system's primary push-notification to the user) plus systematically wrong lastChanged/event dates after any crash day.
findings.suggested_fix: Have detect-changes.js emit a pipeline-health report and add it to EXPECTED_SCRIPTS; alternatively add a freshness probe after the step (fail if alert-state.json lastRun != RUN_DATE_UTC).

findings.title: Stale operational documentation inside live gates (18% vs 13%, 180 vs 240 min)
findings.description: Two operator-facing texts contradict the code they describe. (1) daily-pull.yml:304 emits '::warning::... Letting the coverage gate (n_ok >= max(2500, 18%)) decide' but the actual gate three lines of shell later is max(2500, total*0.13) (Tag 233 recalibration updated the formula, not the warning). (2) monthly-sec-xbrl.yml:8-9 justifies the 08:00 cron with 'daily pull starts at 02:00 UTC with 180-min timeout' — the daily timeout has been 240 min since Tag 219, and observed runs finish 09:16-10:32 UTC, i.e. AFTER the monthly's 08:00 start; only the shared 'main-push' concurrency group (not the cron spacing) actually prevents overlap on the 1st of the month.
findings.mechanism: Comment drift across recalibration tags; the monthly comment encodes a safety argument that is no longer true, hiding the fact that the concurrency group is the only real protection.
findings.reproducer: Compare daily-pull.yml line 304 vs 355; compare monthly comment vs daily-pull.yml:33 and bot commit times (git log --author=yahoo-pull-bot).
findings.impact: Operator reading the warning during an incident applies the wrong threshold; anyone removing/renaming the concurrency group based on the cron-spacing comment reintroduces the 1st-of-month push race.
findings.suggested_fix: Fix the warning string to 13%; update the monthly comment to state that serialization relies on the shared concurrency group, not the schedule gap.

findings.title: Watchlist sanity floor of 200 is 0.8% of the actual universe — gate cannot catch real corruption
findings.description: Verify Watchlist Sanity hard-fails only if size < 200, described as 'manual baseline floor'. The watchlist is now 23,748 stocks. A refresh/prune mishap that destroys 95% of the universe (leaving e.g. 1,200 tickers) sails through, and every downstream artifact (modes report, screener, picks vintages) is silently computed on the remnant — the exact 'stale or degenerate watchlist silently propagates' scenario the F-CI-003 comment says this gate exists to prevent. The floor was never recalibrated through the 13k -> 15.7k -> 23.7k universe growth that the surrounding comments (Tag 227a) document in detail.
findings.mechanism: Absolute floor chosen at a 200-ticker era; both refresh-universe and prune-watchlist run with continue-on-error, so this gate is the ONLY protection, and it triggers ~99% too late.
findings.reproducer: Truncate watchlist.json to 250 stocks; the gate passes; the day's run publishes picks from a 1% universe.
findings.impact: A single bad refresh (e.g. all discovery sources 403 + aggressive prune) produces a green run with garbage universe; picks-history records a poisoned vintage that backtests later consume.
findings.suggested_fix: Relative gate, mirroring the Tag 215e dual-gate precedent: fail if size < max(10000, 0.6 * previous committed size); previous size is available from git HEAD's watchlist.json before the refresh steps overwrite it.

findings.title: Daily cron runs 7 days/week incl. weekends/holidays; top-of-hour 02:00 slot adds delay
findings.description: Market-hours sanity is otherwise good (02:00 UTC is safely after the 20:00/21:00 UTC US close, and data lands ~09:30-10:30 UTC, well before the 13:30/14:30 UTC open). But the cron fires on Saturdays, Sundays and US market holidays too: each weekend burns ~8h of runner time re-pulling quotes that have not changed since Friday's close and produces near-duplicate Sat/Sun vintages in picks-history/methods-history (weekend vintages have ~zero 1-day information; walk-forward week-offset matching must skip them). If the repo is private, the ~7,400 runner-minutes/month this schedule consumes is 3.7x the 2,000-min free tier. Separately, '0 2 * * *' is a top-of-hour slot where GitHub documents heavy cron congestion and start delays; observed bot commit times are consistent with multi-hour start delays.
findings.mechanism: Cron has no weekday filter and no holiday awareness; vintage-producing snapshot scripts run unconditionally.
findings.reproducer: ls picks-history/ - 2026-05-24 (Sun), 2026-05-25 (Mon, Memorial Day), 2026-05-31 (Sun) vintages exist with near-identical content to the prior Friday.
findings.impact: ~30% of compute wasted; weekend vintages dilute walk-forward sample independence; cron-slot congestion delays data availability.
findings.suggested_fix: Use '17 2 * * 2-6' (Tue-Sat UTC = Mon-Fri US trading days, off-peak minute); optionally short-circuit the job when macro-regime/market-calendar marks a holiday.

findings.title: Actions pinned to mutable major tags (@v4), not commit SHAs
findings.description: actions/checkout@v4 and actions/setup-node@v4 are referenced by mutable major tags in a workflow that holds contents:write permission and pushes with the repo GITHUB_TOKEN daily. A compromised or yanked tag (the tj-actions/changed-files class of supply-chain incident) would execute with write access to the data repo on the next 02:00 cron. Node version pinning itself is consistent (22 in both workflows) — only the action refs are mutable.
findings.mechanism: Major tags are repointable by the action publisher; schedule-triggered workflows execute new tag contents with no human in the loop.
findings.impact: Supply-chain exposure for a workflow that can rewrite main and gh-pages.
findings.suggested_fix: Pin to full commit SHAs with a tag comment (e.g. actions/checkout@<sha> # v4.2.x) and let Dependabot bump them.

files_examined: pull-sec-xbrl.js (full pull loop, manifest/304 logic, cache dir)
git history (yahoo-pull-bot commit cadence 2026-05-12..06-12, committed sizes of methods-history/picks-history/score-history/state files)
picks-history/2026-06-12.json as committed by bot (ticker letter distribution)
